correctness.rationale: The independent checker uses the field polynomial x⁴+x+1, last-coordinate normalization for points and complete projective point sets as line keys (rather than row-echelon forms). In the affine chart a second Gröbner order verifies that the gradient ideal contains z⁴+z², x²+x+z²+z, and y²+y+z²+z. Hence even over an algebraic closure singular candidates are binary, and none satisfies the quartic; symmetry covers all charts. The checker tested all 85 and 4369 representatives and found 20 and 554 points. It confirms the 60 lines (geometric completeness from Rams–Schütt), 30 Frobenius pairs, adjacency valency 17 and its stated characteristic polynomial, and ranks 20 and 10 for G and GN. For the sum D of lines, H·D=60 and D²=900; the class D−15H is perpendicular to H with square zero, hence numerically zero by Hodge index. This puts the ample class in the span, making the pairing nondegenerate; pair sums span the fixed part in characteristic zero. The 20 divisor eigenvalues are ten of each ±4. The two remaining traces from the counts are 3 and −23 (first and second powers), hence product 16. The normalized residual roots are reciprocals, so if either were a root of unity both would be, contrary to their nonintegral rational sum 3/4. Divisor classes descend to some finite extension and inject rationally into cohomology, so the residual quotient has no divisor classes. The Picard invariant rank is ten by finite-field descent; the residual 2-adic valuations are 0 and 4, and the divisor valuations are 2, yielding slopes 0,1^20,2 on dividing valuations by 2.
residual_risks: The finite computation checks the explicit model and does not replace standard Hodge index, cycle-class, descent, trace-formula and crystalline comparison facts.
